html:
The herring buss was a broad Dutch fishing ship, first recorded at Hoorn around 1416, that stayed at sea for weeks and gutted, salted and packed its catch in barrels on board.

Herring shoal each summer in the North Sea. Before the buss, fish had to be landed fast before they spoiled. Curing on board meant the Dutch could fish far from home, and their salted herring kept well enough to sell across Europe and the Baltic. Fleets of hundreds of busses sailed each June, with escort ships against pirates and rival navies.

The trade was called the Great Fishery, and people said Amsterdam was built on herring bones. It trained sailors, built ships and created demand for Baltic timber and French and Portuguese salt, which fed the Dutch Republic and its later overseas trade. English and Scottish anger at Dutch boats off their coasts was one cause of the Anglo-Dutch Wars.
sum: The herring buss was a broad Dutch fishing ship, first recorded at Hoorn around 1416, that stayed at sea for weeks and gutted, salted and packed its catch in barrels on board.
